company.name: Pipestream
company.description: A sales engagement platform: reps build email sequences, and Pipestream sends them and tracks replies. Pricing is per seat, so active reps are the metric everyone watches.

title: Pipestream: AI email drafts
brief: Pipestream planned a 35-day test of AI email drafts. After 4 days the result looked so good (+6.7%) that the team stopped it and asked for approval to launch. Read the results and make the call.

hidden.summary: Stopped too early: the test has a fraction of the sample it needs, and the result is not significant.
hidden.explanation: Big early lifts are common in small samples and usually shrink as data comes in. With 6,016 reps per arm, the observed +6.7% has p = 0.187 and a 95% interval of −3.2% to +16.5%: it is compatible with no effect at all. Stopping as soon as the result 'looks good' (peeking) inflates false positives. The split and the guardrail are fine; the problem is that there is not enough data to decide.

issueNotes.underpowered: The plan needed 47,034 reps per arm to detect a 5% lift, and the test stopped at 6,016. The 95% interval (−3.2% to +16.5%) includes zero and effects far smaller than the one the team is celebrating.

hidden.recommendation: Resume the test and let it run to the planned sample (47,034 per arm) before deciding. Agree on the stopping rule before the test starts, not while watching the numbers.

experiment.name: AI email drafts
experiment.change: The sequence editor offers an AI-written first draft of each email, based on the prospect's company and role.
experiment.hypothesis: Reps who do not have to start from a blank page will launch more sequences.

primaryMetric.label: Sequence launch rate
primaryMetric.description: Share of active reps who launch at least one email sequence that day.

guardrails.label: Prospect replies
guardrails.description: Share of launched sequences that get a reply.
